Definition: to be rancid, i.e. (transitively) to loathe
BiblicalUsage: zâham means to be rancid, that is (transitively) to loathe. In Job 33:20 we read, "So that his life abhorreth bread, and his soul dainty meat."
TheologicalSignificance: zaham is to be rancid, that is (transitively) to loathe, and I hold that a small word can carry a large truth when God speaks it.
